newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Shell sets 2.8 bln peso 1997 capex.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Shell sets 2.8 bln peso 1997 capex.

text.p: Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp, a unit of Royal Dutch/Shell group of companies, said on Tuesday it has earmarked 2.8 billion pesos in capital expenditures for 1997.

Pilipinas Shell president Oscar Reyes told Reuters in an interview that the amount will be used to upgrade its refinery and distribution facilities and the continued expansion of its service stations.
Reyes said this year's capital expenditure would be used partly for the construction of 50 new retail stations and upgrading of 40 existing ones.

Commenting on earnings for the year, Reyes said: "We will likely be slightly higher than 1996. It's a volatile situation because this will be the first time that we are operating in a deregulated environment."
The oil industry was fully deregulated in February.
"We aim to maintain our market share. Given that the oil industry has deregulated, it's a tall order to do so," said Reyes. Pilipinas Shell has 33.7 percent of the market, second to Petron Corp.
It earlier reported 2.52 billion peso net income in 1996 from 1.69 billion the previous year. The company had set aside 2.5 billion pesos in capital expenditure in 1996.
Reyes said Shell is reducing its workforce by 10 percent this year to a little over 1,000 as part of a company reorganisation.
